Resident Evil 7 - Does It Hold Up?

When RE7 first came out, it had a very positive reception from fans and critics alike. It may have been because the game is stunningly beautiful or because the departure from formula breathed some much needed life into the franchise. Upon a second playthrough two years later, I fund myself asking, "Is this game as good as I thought it was?"

Even two years later, the graphics and level design hold up tremendously, but many cracks have started to show through. For starters, the game seems to have a "because everyone is stupid" plot. You'd think that upon noticing a totem made of horse corpses and buzz saws, Ethan would turn around and get the police involved. You can argue "well, if we do that, we can't have a game", but that's not true. It makes for a creepy image, but was it necessary to place it so early in the game?

Many horror games, like Silent Hill, have a reason why the protagonist cannot leave. In Ethan's case, he appears to be equal parts stubborn or stupid.

Other things I noticed were that, aside from Mia, the English dub has some pretty rough voice acting. Ethan is completely flat, whereas the hillbilly family is hamming it up. An intentional juxtaposition, perhaps?

There are several scripted events with only one way to proceed, and that way is not always clear. This leads to many deaths that feel unfair. It's especially jarring when the death is in a video flashback and the result is inevitable anyway.

I sat down with my friend Andy and we reviewed the game again to see if it holds up. I hope you enjoy.
